newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Debris found, search resumes for Sri Lanka plane.
newsitem.headline: Debris found, search resumes for Sri Lanka plane.

text.p: The Sri Lankan military spotted unidentified debris in waters off the Jaffna Peninsula while searching for a missing air force surveillance plane, a senior air force official said on Tuesday.

But the debris could not be retrieved and the navy and air force resumed their joint search for the Chinese-built Y-12 airplane, missing off northern Sri Lanka since early Monday, the official said. The twin-propeller aircraft had a crew of four.
"They have spied some wreckage. But the light was fast fading at that time (Monday evening) and they were forced to come in. They resumed their search at first light on Tuesday," the official said.

Air force planes and helicopters, joined by navy patrol boats, were to continue their search for the plane, last seen about 75 miles (120 km) east of the military's northern Palaly air base, the official added.
The 14-seat aircraft was looking for a suspected Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) ship when it lost radio contact with the ground around 5.15 a.m. (2315 GMT) on Monday.

It was the second time in recent days that an air force plane had disappeared. Last week, an unmanned air force drone used for reconnaissance was lost over the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
A rebel statement last Saturday said "an unmanned spy plane" had crashed in the Pooneryn area south of the Jaffna Peninsula last week "due to apparent mechanical failure".

But the LTTE, which is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, has so far not commented on the disappearance of the Y-12 aircraft.
The rebels, meanwhile, ambushed an army patrol near Valachchenai in eastern Batticaloa district on Monday evening, killing seven soldiers and wounding one, a Defence Ministry official said.
The government has said that more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
